hypotheses.claim: Adding a dimensionless endpoint demand-balance term (1 - |q_i-q_j|/(q_i+q_j)) on top of the scale-normalized generalized savings + capacity-fill score strictly improves dev_24 mean tour length relative to pure fill-weighted savings (16.1921), because it reduces tail-fragment routes by pairing comparable-demand endpoints; and EoH perturbing lam in [1.00,1.20], mu in [0.05,0.20], beta_fill in [0.0,0.20], beta_balance in [0.0,0.12] will find a strictly better static merge rule without any budget-exhaustion risk (p95 stays <5ms of 25ms).

next_search_advice.direction: Refine the scale-normalized generalized savings merge score with the balanced-fill variant (lam≈1.08, mu≈0.12, beta_fill≈0.10, beta_balance≈0.05) and let EoH co-evolve the four dimensionless coefficients (lam, mu, beta_fill, beta_balance, plus scale divisor choice) rather than hard-coding, keeping the one-shot vectorized evaluation to preserve the sub-4ms p95 at the 25ms budget.
